CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old female presents for routine follow-up. Recently started on Buspar by Dr. Brown for anxiety management. She experienced significant anxiety in November and December, initially manifesting as premenstrual exacerbation before progressing to random anxiety episodes during work hours. Patient attributes anxiety to multiple factors: work-related stress from leading COVID patient result delivery process and opening evaluation/COVID clinics, hormonal changes on progesterone for menstrual regulation, and possible side effect from Singulair (per Dr. Ward's warning that Singulair can cause anxiety). Anxiety has significantly improved since starting Buspar. She discontinued Camila birth control due to markedly increased appetite while on it, with appetite normalizing after discontinuation. Reports weight loss over past 6 months. Denies other acute concerns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Psychiatric: Anxiety well-controlled on Buspar
Gastrointestinal: Increased hunger on birth control, resolved after discontinuation
Constitutional: Weight loss over 6 months
Breast: Lumps/nodules present, smaller than before; left-sided tenderness
Gynecologic: Vulvovaginal itching/discomfort managed with topical cream once weekly
Other systems: Reviewed and negative

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Abnormal pap smear circa 2009 requiring surveillance every 6 months, subsequently normalized
- Benign breast lumps/cysts
- History of breastfeeding with clogged duct

MEDICATIONS
- Buspar (newly started)
- Progesterone
- Singulair
- Topical vaginal cream (once weekly)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother: Breast cancer diagnosed at approximately age 45

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in healthcare involved in COVID response efforts. Married with children (son and daughter). Patient and son vaccinated against COVID; husband and daughter vaccine-hesitant. History of breastfeeding.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Neck: Small palpable nodules noted, smaller than at previous exam
Breast: Left breast with slight increased density and tenderness; palpable nodules/lumps present, smaller than previous but still present
Pelvic: Normal external genitalia

RESULTS
Pap smear (2019): Negative/negative
Pap smear: Ordered today

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety disorder: Significantly improved on Buspar. Discussed multiple contributing factors including work stress, hormonal changes, and age-related factors. Continue Buspar. Monitor for recurrence.

2. Breast lumps and nodules: Likely benign etiology (cysts, fibroadenomas). Patient expressed concern given mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 45. Reassured that malignancy would demonstrate changes on exam and patient is under appropriate surveillance. Referral placed to breast specialist for ongoing surveillance, in-office ultrasound, and procedural capability if needed. Specialist will contact within couple of business days to schedule appointment.

3. Gynecologic cancer prevention:
   - Pap smear repeat ordered today (last screening 2019, negative; prior abnormal pap 2009; repeat indicated given history and potential increased risk from immunocompromise, stress, and vaccine exposure)
   - Continue progesterone for menstrual regulation
   - Refill topical vaginal cream for vulvovaginal itching

4. Follow-up: Patient to schedule with breast specialist. Call with any questions or concerns.
